stem.text: An organic compound, X, has the composition shown.
The infrared spectrum of X is shown.

stem.alt: Infrared spectrum: transmittance / % (0 to 100) against wavenumber / cm–1 from 4000 to about 450. The trace is near 90% from 4000 to about 3050 with no broad absorption. There is a sharp absorption at about 2980 (down to about 35%). The baseline is flat from about 2900 to 1800. Very strong sharp absorptions occur at about 1740 (down to about 5%) and about 1240 (about 5%), with further strong absorptions near 1370 (about 20%) and 1050 (about 12%), a medium one near 1450, and several smaller peaks below 1000.

explanation.text: Empirical formula: C 54.54/12.0 = 4.545, H 9.09/1.0 = 9.09, O 36.37/16.0 = 2.273 (Ar(O) from the Periodic Table). Dividing by 2.273 gives C : H : O = 2 : 4 : 1, so the empirical formula is C2H4O. Butanoic acid and ethyl ethanoate (both C4H8O2) fit; ethanoic acid and methyl methanoate (both C2H4O2, empirical formula CH2O) do not.

The spectrum has no broad O–H absorption between 2500 and 3000 cm<sup>–1</sup>, so X is not a carboxylic acid. The strong sharp absorption near 1740 cm<sup>–1</sup> (C=O, ester range 1710–1750) and the strong absorptions near 1240 and 1050 cm<sup>–1</sup> (C–O) point to an ester.

optionAnalysis.text: The empirical formula fits (C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>2</sub>), but a carboxylic acid would show a very broad O–H absorption from 2500 to 3000 cm<sup>–1</sup>, which is absent.
Ethanoic acid, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>2</sub>, has empirical formula CH<sub>2</sub>O (40.0% C), and it would also show a broad O–H absorption.
Ethyl ethanoate, C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>2</sub>, matches the 2 : 4 : 1 ratio; its spectrum shows ester C=O near 1740 and C–O near 1240 cm<sup>–1</sup>, with no O–H.
Methyl methanoate is an ester, but C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>2</sub> gives 40.0% C, not 54.54%.

reasoningChain: Moles ratio C : H : O = 4.545 : 9.09 : 2.273 = 2 : 4 : 1, so empirical formula C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O.
Only the C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>2</sub> options fit: butanoic acid (A) or ethyl ethanoate (C).
No broad O–H at 2500–3000 cm<sup>–1</sup>: not a carboxylic acid.
C=O at about 1740 and C–O at about 1240 cm<sup>–1</sup>: an ester, ethyl ethanoate.

inferredMistakes.text: Reading the sharp C–H absorption near 2980 cm<sup>–1</sup> as the carboxyl O–H band and choosing butanoic acid.
Skipping the composition data and choosing between the four compounds on the IR spectrum alone, which cannot separate the two esters.
